match.reason: The new point teaches both the mean and median (centre) and the range and IQR (spread) together, but no bank point covers both: mat-measures-centre has only centre, mat-measures-spread and mat-spread-box-plots have only spread, and the spread card also goes beyond Foundation level into standard deviation.

draft.title: Mean, median and spread
card: Mean
Add all the values, then divide by how many there are. Example: 2, 4, 9 has a mean of 15 ÷ 3 = 5.
Median
Put the values in order and take the middle one. With two middle values, take the number halfway between them. For 2, 4, 9 the median is 4.
Range
Range = highest value − lowest value. For 2, 4, 9 the range is 9 − 2 = 7.
IQR
The interquartile range (IQR) = Q3 − Q1, the spread of the middle half of the data. A very high or low value changes the mean and range a lot, but changes the median and IQR much less.
draft.remember: Mean and median give a typical value. Range and IQR give the spread.

a.q: What is the mean of these quiz scores: 4, 7, 5, 8, 6?
a.why: Add the scores: 4 + 7 + 5 + 8 + 6 = 30. Divide by 5 scores to get 6. The answer 30 is only the total, and the division step has been skipped.
a.clue: Add them up, then divide by how many scores there are.

b.q: Five houses in a street sold for $500 000, $520 000, $540 000, $560 000 and $2 400 000. Which measure is changed least by the $2.4 million sale, and what is its value?
b.why: The middle of the five ordered prices is $540 000, and the very high sale does not move it. The mean is $904 000 and the range is $1 900 000, and both are pulled up a lot by that one sale.
b.clue: Which measure is the middle value, not one pulled by a large value?

problems.detail: The clue 'Which measure is the middle value...' tells students the answer is the median, so they can pick it without reasoning about how outliers affect each measure.
The IQR is given as Q3 − Q1, but the card never says what Q1 and Q3 (the quartiles) are or how to find them, so students meeting the term here cannot use it.

proposal.title: Mean, median and spread
card: Mean
Add all the values, then divide by how many there are. Example: 2, 4, 9 has a mean of 15 ÷ 3 = 5.
Median
Put the values in order and take the middle one. With two middle values, take the number halfway between them. For 2, 4, 9 the median is 4.
Range
Range = highest value − lowest value. For 2, 4, 9 it is 9 − 2 = 7. One very high or low value changes the mean and range a lot, but the median and IQR much less.
IQR
Split the ordered data into a lower and upper half. Q1 is the median of the lower half, Q3 the median of the upper half, and IQR = Q3 − Q1. For 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12: Q1 = 4, Q3 = 10, IQR = 6.
